name.description: The full name of the RestorePlan Resource.
name.rationale: Resource identification has no direct security impact but is essential for governance and operational management of restore plans.

backup_plan.description: A reference to the BackupPlan from which Backups may be used as the source for Restores created via this RestorePlan.
backup_plan.rationale: Defines the source of backup data for restore operations. Must reference approved backup plans to ensure data integrity and compliance with backup policies.

cluster.description: The source cluster from which Restores will be created via this RestorePlan.
cluster.rationale: Defines where backup data will be restored. Must reference approved target clusters to prevent unauthorized data restoration to unmanaged environments.

restore_config.description: Defines the configuration of Restores created via this RestorePlan. Structure is [documented below](#nested_restore_config).
restore_config.rationale: CRITICAL: Controls what data is restored and how restoration is performed. Improper configuration can lead to security vulnerabilities, data exposure, or service disruption.

namespaced_resource_restore_mode.description: Defines the behavior for handling the situation where sets of namespaced resources being restored already exist in the target cluster. This MUST be set to a value other than `NAMESPACED_RESOURCE_RESTORE_MODE_UNSPECIFIED` if the `namespacedResourceRestoreScope` is anything other than `noNamespaces`. See https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/reference/rest/v1/RestoreConfig#namespacedresourcerestoremode for more information on each mode. Possible values are: `DELETE_AND_RESTORE`, `FAIL_ON_CONFLICT`, `MERGE_SKIP_ON_CONFLICT`, `MERGE_REPLACE_VOLUME_ON_CONFLICT`, `MERGE_REPLACE_ON_CONFLICT`.
namespaced_resource_restore_mode.rationale: Controls how conflicts are resolved during restore. Different modes have varying security implications for existing data and configurations. FAIL_ON_CONFLICT is safest.

volume_data_restore_policy.description: Specifies the mechanism to be used to restore volume data. This should be set to a value other than `NAMESPACED_RESOURCE_RESTORE_MODE_UNSPECIFIED` if the `namespacedResourceRestoreScope` is anything other than `noNamespaces`. If not specified, it will be treated as `NO_VOLUME_DATA_RESTORATION`. See https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/reference/rest/v1/RestoreConfig#VolumeDataRestorePolicy for more information on each policy option. Possible values are: `RESTORE_VOLUME_DATA_FROM_BACKUP`, `REUSE_VOLUME_HANDLE_FROM_BACKUP`, `NO_VOLUME_DATA_RESTORATION`.
volume_data_restore_policy.rationale: Controls how persistent volume data is restored. Must balance recovery needs with security considerations for sensitive data.

cluster_resource_conflict_policy.description: Defines the behavior for handling the situation where cluster-scoped resources being restored already exist in the target cluster. This MUST be set to a value other than `CLUSTER_RESOURCE_CONFLICT_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED` if `clusterResourceRestoreScope` is anyting other than `noGroupKinds`. See https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/add-on/backup-for-gke/reference/rest/v1/RestoreConfig#clusterresourceconflictpolicy for more information on each policy option. Possible values are: `USE_EXISTING_VERSION`, `USE_BACKUP_VERSION`.
cluster_resource_conflict_policy.rationale: Controls how cluster-level conflicts are resolved. Incorrect settings can affect cluster security configurations. USE_EXISTING_VERSION is safer.

location.description: The region of the Restore Plan.
location.rationale: Determines data residency for restore operations. Must align with approved regions for compliance with data protection regulations.

labels.description: Description: A set of custom labels supplied by the user. A list of key->value pairs. Example: { "name": "wrench", "mass": "1.3kg", "count": "3" }. **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration. Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Essential for governance, security classification, and policy enforcement. Proper labeling enables automated security controls and compliance auditing for restore operations.

project.description: If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project context for resource creation, typically inherited from provider configuration.
